title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: review set limit per case rises from 20 to 100 (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: the Graph call is documented to change a case's type, but the sources do not establish that it enables or disables premium features as the controls table promises. The higher limit, licensing prerequisites and other control paths are supported; two descriptive assertions also need narrowing.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding search results to a review set copies items from their original data sources.
claims.quote: All items in the search results are copied from the original data source in the live services to a secure Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud.

claims.claim: The copied material includes the items' metadata.
claims.quote: When you add content to a review set, the items and their metadata are copied to a Microsoft-managed Azure Storage location dedicated to the case.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Review set storage is Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed Azure Storage dedicated to the case.
claims.quote: The storage is Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed. ... the items and their metadata are copied to a Microsoft-managed Azure Storage location dedicated to the case.

claims.claim: Storage is provisioned per case and shared by the case's review sets.
claims.quote: Storage is provisioned per case. Multiple review sets within the same case share the underlying case storage, with logical separation so each review set's content remains independently queryable, taggable, and exportable.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: eDiscovery permissions govern access to case and review set data.
claims.quote: This role lets users access review sets in eDiscovery. Users who are assigned this role can see and open the list of cases that they're members of.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators can access case data for any case in the organisation.
claims.quote: Access case data for any case in the organization.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Administrators must add themselves as case members to manage a case.
claims.quote: Manage any eDiscovery case after they add themselves as a member of the case.

claims.claim: Access to review set content is through the Microsoft Purview portal and approved export workflows.
claims.quote: Access to review set content is only through the Microsoft Purview portal and approved export workflows.

claims.claim: There is no customer-accessible storage URL or account key for review set content.
claims.quote: There's no customer-accessible SAS token, account key, or storage URL for review set content.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: In a data spillage scenario, the only way to remove items from a review set is to delete the case.
claims.quote: In data spillage scenarios, the only way to remove items in a review set is to delete the eDiscovery case. Other search and purge methods don't remove items from a review set.

claims.claim: Deleting the containing case is required to delete a review set and its data.
claims.quote: You can't delete items from a review set, and you can't delete review sets from a case. To delete a review set and its data, you must delete the eDiscovery case that contains the review set.

claims.claim: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage cases they create.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.

claims.claim: The Reviewer role group's review access is limited to data in review sets.
claims.quote: This role doesn't allow the user to preview the results of a search that's associated with the case or do other search or case management tasks. Users with this role can only access the data in a review set.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Existing eDiscovery Manager, Administrator and Reviewer permissions provide case-management and review-access controls.
claims.quote: Members can also create and manage cases ... and access case data. ... Review | ... eDiscovery Manager & Administrator ... Reviewer

claims.claim: People can create review sets while adding search results.
claims.quote: Select a search on the Searches tab, and then select Add to review set. ... select Add to a new review set or Add to an existing review set.

claims.claim: The higher limit does not create anything on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery review sets 20 limit split extra cases same investigation automatic create review sets; eDiscovery review sets 100 automatically default. Opened edisc-search-add-to-review-set, edisc-review-set-manage and the roadmap record; none explicitly states this negative.
claims.fix: Replace 'the higher limit does not create anything on its own' with 'the roadmap describes a limit increase, not an automatic creation workflow'. The supplied roadmap description states only that the limit rises from 20 to 100.

claims.quote: Adding data to a review set is a long-running process that includes gathering items from the original data sources in Microsoft 365 ... copying them to the Azure Storage location ... and then reindexing the items.

claims.claim: The add-to-review-set process can be tracked on Process manager.
claims.quote: You can track the progress on the Process manager page.

claims.claim: Organisation-wide concurrent-process limits still apply.
claims.quote: Maximum number of concurrent processes in your organization. | 50 | 200

claims.claim: Organisation-wide daily-job limits still apply.

claims.fix: Replace 'With a ceiling of 20, teams had to open extra cases for the same matter' with 'For teams that split a matter across cases to stay below 20 review sets, the higher limit may simplify case organisation'. claims.claim: The rating none concerns the increased case limit within existing premium entitlement, not all possible review-set data-storage costs.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table

claims.fix: The 'Include review set count in case close-out checks' and 'Watch cases approaching the 40 million documents per case' checklist steps have no corresponding control row. Remove those two steps; do not add unverified control rows.
